flags.summary: The prospect disclosed that a CrossFit injury damaged his lower back to the point he can no longer perform barbell squats, and he made this disclosure after his card had already been charged for a loaded kettlebell programme; the rep responded with two words and moved on to a different topic.
evidence: I was doing CrossFit, so many injuries. Yeah, CrossFit up my lower back pretty bad, so that's why I don't do CrossFit anymore. I can't squat, I can't do barbell squats anymore, actually, because of it.
Oh, damn.
Hey, give me one sec, I need to grab my credit card.
Oh, okay. I see it went through.

flags.summary: The injuries question was asked once and answered dismissively, and the rep accepted it without probing, despite the prospect saying in the same breath that he regularly injures himself and expects to again.
evidence: Okay, so we know what's going on in terms of you moving around. How about injuries? Anything?
I was having a little bit of stuff in my shoulder, but the chiropractor really figured that out. Honestly, man, I'm pretty good.
For a little bit, because of jiu-jitsu, I couldn't run. I run sometimes, too. I couldn't run because of my knees, but that's fine now, too.
So yeah, I think I'm good now, but that could change any day, because I sometimes mess myself up from jiu-jitsu.

flags.summary: The deal closed at $4,000 for three months, a tier that does not exist in the stated offer, after the rep cut the price from $6,000 within roughly four minutes of the prospect mentioning competing holiday spend — and after the prospect had already confirmed he could afford the full price.
evidence: So, as I said, Trevor is working for six months, and that investment is 6K.
I have, I definitely have the money. It's more, it's more like, it's just more than I thought it was going to be.
The only thing is just the timing, because I got a trip to Europe coming up, and then I've got a jujitsu camp coming up, and those are both pretty expensive.
Tell you what? There's a three-month option that you could do, because for the three months, it's going to be 4K.
Okay, cool. Let's do that. I like that.

flags.summary: The prospect was steered onto the three-month tier without being told that the six-month tier carries a performance guarantee and the three-month tier does not — a term the same rep described the same week as the defining difference between them.
evidence: Tell you what? There's a three-month option that you could do, because for the three months, it's going to be 4K. But after those three months, you can go still for additional three months and have it like a full six months, and you'll just need to pay the rest of the MO.

Just for the information, the six months is the full transformation with a guarantee. With three months, there is no guarantee because it's too short of a time to guarantee (Suman call, 1f48fSQ33WjpakBuD5qucuBvySRs-YkxZ, 00:30:58)
Trevor is going to be working with you until you do hit that for free (Suman call, same date)

flags.summary: Three financed configurations were quoted as monthly figures only — $2,300, $1,200 and $650 per month, totalling $6,900, $7,200 and $7,800 against a $6,000 price — and when the prospect asked directly for the interest rate he was given more monthly figures instead of a rate.
evidence: Like we can use the financing option too, like the third party, and you can split it even into like 12-month installments, but that's with an interest too, yeah?
Do you know what the interest rate is with Paybook?
So if you would like to split it, for example, over three months, that would be 2,300 per month.
And that's the same, if you split it in six months, that would be $1,200, and for 12 months, $650.

flags.summary: A same-call decision deadline was applied, framed around the rep's schedule and an unwillingness to chase — the same phrasing this rep used on another call in this batch, indicating a repeated pattern rather than a one-off.
evidence: When do you need an answer, Mike?
20 minutes, you need an answer today?
I don't want to chase you down.
We have a busy schedule, so, you know.
Look, my schedule is pretty busy, and I don't want to play Chase. So let's lock it in. (Maz call, 1WSNJRG8mX9-BpVOc0kuYGmAOwe1ATjMm, 00:32:55)

flags.summary: The rep again used identifying details of other named-by-description clients and prospects as social proof, a repeat of the same pattern on another call the same day.
evidence: like I had a 59-year-old Jiu-Jitsu guy just three days ago, and that's his main thing. Like he, over the years, he grew like almost a hunchback.

It reminds me of a guy that I had a few weeks back, like almost 60, businessman, he was a former athlete... he told me one thing, that he wants to be in such a good shape that when he enters a business meeting, he's looking at all the guys, he wants to feel that he can crush every single one of them.
Somebody was referring to that like five calls ago
